newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Glaverbel says 1996 group net profit rises.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Glaverbel says 1996 group net profit rises.

text.p: Belgian glass maker Glaverbel said on Thursday group net profit more than doubled in 1996, boosted by extraordinaries, but operating profit suffered after volumes and glass prices dropped in the first half of last year.
In 1997 the company expected to see improved operating results, and a further decrease in its financial charges through debt control and the impact of low interest rates.
"Given the continuing upturn in European glass consumption and assuming prices hold up the group anticipates an improvement in its operating result in 1997," it said in a statement.
Chief executive officer Luc Willame told a news conference that Glaverbel was "reasonably confident" for 1997.
"Unless there's something new on the currency front or a big price drop, there should be an improvement in profit," he added.
In 1996 Glaverbel's operating profit fell 8.5 percent to 2.73 billion francs ($78.4 million) after recession in the first half of last year when raw glass volumes and prices fell to historic lows.
The second half saw quantities recovering significantly but there was no improvement in prices.
The group said operating results in 1997 would be helped by growth in European glass consumption estimated at two percent overall, and expected to be strong in the automotive sector.

Willame said the 1996 price drop - of 10 to 20 percent for raw glass in Europe - had wiped one billion francs off turnover, which edged up one percent (1.6 percent on a comparable consolidation basis) to 38.66 billion francs.
However most of this negative effect was clawed back via increased volume, productivity and cost control. The recovery of some weaker currencies also helped offset the price fall.
Group net profit rose to 1.768 billion francs from 621 million in 1995, after extraordinary profit of 606 million.
This included a previously announced net capital gain of 1.166 billion francs from the sale last August of Glaverbel's stake in U.S. glass group AFG Industries.
Glaverbel said net financial expenditure fell to 1.3 billion in 1996 from 2.2 billion in 1995.
The company is controlled by Japan's Asahi Glass Co.

Glaverbel's debt to equity ratio stood at 0.72 at the end of 1996 (0.63 after deducting debt represented by the group's treasury shares) after the various acquisitions and divestments during the year, down from 0.97 at the end of 1995.
Net debt at the end of 1996 was 14.5 billion francs, down from 21 billion at the end of 1995.
Future investments would focus on providing "added value", now its past modernisation programme was beginning to pay off.

Generally, Glaverbel said its strategy was to "grow in a profitable way" according to its financial resources, and to diversify more geographically. It also had to tackle low profitability in its processing activities, especially in Belgium which suffered high labour costs. ($ = 34.82 Belgian Francs)
